setting.region: The Hollow Coast, a tidal estuary and low wooded dunes
world_facts: A freshwater seep emerges behind the northern dune
Tidal flats supply shellfish and shallow-water fish
Thin stands of scrubwood grow inland beyond the sand
During the last two high tides the spring water has tasted faintly salty

The lower stone-lined spring catchment tastes brackish around the highest tides; water gathered from a trickle further upslope tasted fresh during the six-day observation period, but adequacy and long-term safety are unverified.

A wooded, wind-sheltered upper dune bench north-northeast of camp has firmer root-bound ground and no visible recent wave debris; building there would require hauling materials and verifying a dependable water route.
A second dune saddle has exposed shifting sand and is not a favored shelter site.

Over ten autumn days, the upper trickle continued tasting fresh even when the lower catchment was brackish; water carried on repeated household collection runs met observed needs at current flow, but longer-term yield and unseen contamination are not established.
The council built a raised stone and reed draw point and a drainage groove to avoid using the lower tidal catchment; a marked path allows carrying water to twelve high-dune residents.
Timber gatherers report that the easiest fallen wood near the camp is thinning; future fuel gains may require longer journeys.
Early Autumn Days 26-35, additional fuel crews used deadwood along longer routes into the fringe without cutting live trees; nearest deadwood continued to thin.
Three reed gatherers collected fifteen reed bundles from upper lagoon margins; some newly cut reeds remain drying before construction use.
A brisk squall on Day 31 tested improved roofing and drainage: the high-dune shelters held; one older shelter seam briefly leaked and was patched. No residents displaced.
Days 36-45 brought scattered rain but no damaging storm; the upper spring draw point stayed usable, and the lower catchment remained unsuitable at high tide.
Longer trips into already known inland woodland fringe provide sufficient deadwood for maintenance but at growing labor cost; no new regions explored.
Two spare coils of plant-fiber cordage were produced from older cured reed/rush fibers with adult craft labor. More recent reeds still require drying.

During a seven-day inland survey beginning on Day 46, Tovan and three scouts crossed the previously unmapped scrub fringe northwest of Taluma, followed a firm gravel rise, and reached a wooded swale with more fallen timber and living mixed trees than near the coast. The swale is roughly one outward day of walking in good weather from Taluma; carrying bulky fuel back over sandy dunes substantially slows the return.

Scouts marked a route from the familiar woodland fringe to the inland swale using cairns and conspicuous forked branches. This is a reconnaissance path, not a cleared wagon track or secured supply line.

Scouts observed healthy saplings, larger trees and some deadfall, suggesting prospects for carefully managed wood gathering, but a single visit cannot measure annual regrowth or guarantee winter access. No large wood shipments were brought from the newly identified swale.

On one fallen trunk in the swale, Tovan noted weathered tool-like chopping marks older than the party’s arrival. The origin and age are unknown; this is not evidence of a confirmed neighboring settlement.

Days 56-65: A small team cleared brush and marked firmer stepping places on the surveyed northwest corridor. The route remains a narrow and uneven footpath rather than a dependable all-weather supply line.

Two primitive hand-carried wooden timber frames were tested on a short relay leg. Dry deadwood equivalent to about one settlement-day of fuel was delivered and included in stocks, but the frame design and true labor savings remain unproven.

Near the previously marked fallen trunk, surveyors recovered a pair of struck stone flakes among older leaf debris and identified several weathered chopping scars consistent with past tool use. No securely dated site or identifiable living group was found. Do not assume the inland woodland is unowned or abandoned.

A small experimental hearth with a stone draft shield and wind baffle was constructed. It appears to shelter flames from wind, but no controlled fuel-consumption trial has demonstrated material savings; ordinary settlement fuel demand remains unchanged for accounting.

Days 66-75: Four scouts led by Tovan continued beyond the previously mapped wooded swale and found a shallow, stony inland stream running along a low slope. Its flow and drinking-water quality across seasons are untested; the river route is not a Taluma supply line.

Near the inland stream the scouting party saw a short worn foot passage, a small sheltered patch of cold ash bordered with several deliberately placed stones, and an indistinct humanlike track in damp sediment. The age and maker remain unknown; no person, community, territory or ownership claim was confirmed.

Controlled comparative trial of six paired cooking tasks, in similar breezy conditions, suggested that Taluma’s single draft-baffled prototype used about 10-15% less dry wood than an open hearth for the same tasks. The sample is small and wind-dependent; no village-wide consumption change has been applied.

The permanent Council of the Shore began voluntary teaching rotations in fiberwork, food preservation and water care, with two adult apprentices on projects, elders/skill-holders teaching, and some older children observing age-appropriate lessons.

Days 76-85: Tovan led four peaceful scouts back to the stony inland stream. Beside the earlier cold-ash setting they noticed recent-looking snapped shoots and worked fiber, and from across the stream briefly saw two unknown adults; no speech understood, no threatening approach, trade, encampment, territorial claim, or identification. Evidence suggests living people visit the stream but their origin and land rights remain unknown.

Days 76-85: On three separate mornings the inland stream carried a narrow but continuous current over gravel and no brackish taste was reported; one observation followed light rain. Seasonal persistence and invisible contamination remain unknown, and no transfer route or settlement freshwater infrastructure was built.

Days 76-85: Two additional small stone-and-wet-earth baffled cooking hearths were built using two stone loads. Repeated paired cooking comparisons showed modest but variable dry-wood reductions in wind, and one test smoked heavily in damp conditions. All three are local prototypes; no change to general settlement fuel consumption rate is justified.

Days 76-85: Two adults examined seeds of local wild grasses, tested soil and water retention near the settlement away from the protected seep, and prepared two hand-sized experimental sowing patches using gathered seeds rather than protected seed. No germination, domesticated crop, stored harvest, or field-scale agriculture yet.
Days 119-120: an early winter coastal squall brought rain and shifting wind, temporarily interrupting offshore fishing and producing one minor shelter roof leak; no families displaced.

Day 160: Third six-person high-dune shelter completed using mature poles and cured reeds, increasing capacity to 73 with no population change or new permanent settlement. Emergency materials safeguarded.

Day 167: Three unidentified adults approached Taluma along the inland footpath and stopped at a distance from the outer shelters. One wore an ochre-red wrist band like the person seen during earlier stream contact. They displayed a tied woven-fiber loop and placed a closed bundle down, apparently seeking contact. No mutually understood words or claims are established; they have not entered Taluma.

Day 224: With user authorization, Esha, Tovan and Vessa approached the ochre-cord woodland marker peacefully from Taluma’s side, without crossing, making a territorial claim or taking inland timber. Two inland watchers met them at the line. One demonstratively blocked a stick reaching past the cord, pressed an open palm toward the marked woods, then indicated a clearer trail bending toward the inland stream. These gestures strongly suggest that crossing the corded route is unwelcome, and that contact along the stream route may be possible; ownership, territory extent, language and motive remain unestablished. They acknowledged Vessa’s display of the ochre woven token from earlier contact. No trade terms or treaty concluded; parties departed peacefully and the Taluman delegation returned.

Days 321-362: Coastal scouts under Letha identified Shellbend Cove beyond the southern headland, with sheltered tidal shallows, clay seams, dangerous offshore shoals, and possibly maintained low-tide stone fish barriers. No settlement encountered, no assertion that cove is empty or Taluman territory.

Days 321-362: The north-dune seep continued serving 67 residents and both occupied high-dune households. Summer flow was lower on eight dry days but remained adequate with careful gathering; continued vulnerability to a prolonged drought.

At the first turn of the year (Year 2 Day 1), Taluma counted its first full seasonal cycle. No artificial seasonal holiday, legal change, birth or migration was assumed, but Esha asked the families to recall their first winter and chronicle it orally.

Year 2 Days 13-20: Inland visitors freely accepted an invitation and visited Taluma’s communal work area for a nonbinding craft demonstration. Vessa and Iren showed strand twisting and repair, and one inland craftsperson demonstrated adding crushed temper to clay and carefully shaping a small vessel. The inland people departed with their own vessel. A Taluman trial cup subsequently cracked while drying. No finished ceramic technology or formal teaching contract.

Year 2 Days 18-25: Letha observed a group of at least three people returning at two low tides to rearrange stones and empty a small fish trap at Shellbend Cove. The site is actively worked, not abandoned. They were aware of watchers and one gave an open-hand gesture before returning to work; Taluman scouts did not approach or disrupt the weir. Their community name, size and connection to inland neighbors remain unverified.

Year 2 Days 1-32: protected north-dune seep continued supplying all 67 people and the two adults living in the newer high-dune dwelling. No long-drought reliability or safe potable chemistry can be assured.

Year 2 Days 43-57: Letha and two companions approached the outer margin of actively worked Shellbend Cove fish-weir on low tide and used open hands, held-out cordage, and patience to meet two fishers face to face. The fishers kept strangers outside their work zone; Letha complied. A nonbinding single exchange of a coil of Taluman cordage for a worked shell scraper occurred. There was no invitation to fish, trespass, use the cove clay, or establish a binding agreement.

Year 2 Days 48-67: Vessa, Iren and Arel improved tempering, slower shade drying and gradual open-air firing of small hand-built vessels with local Taluma clay. Of seven attempts, two survived low-fire cooling intact; one is slightly porous and holds liquid only briefly. These are real prototypes, not reliable sealed food stores. One additional settlement-fuel-day equivalent used for firing trials.

Year 2 Days 39-71: Maro and Vessa established the Circle of Witnesses, a repeated oral recitation each moon cycle. A small tally cord and seasonal tidal marker board serve only as mnemonic aids, not full writing or an exact calendar. Accounts explicitly distinguish what a person saw from what someone told them. At the first recount, two elder memories differed on the first great storm; the differing versions were preserved rather than silently merged.

Year 2 Days 33-74: Sora compared the first beds as they headed to seed. The dark mulched bed produced viable seed for more trials, the well-drained bed a modest sample, and the sand bed largely failed. Sample withheld for future sowing, not counted as village food. Rema continues private supportive care, with visible signs consistent with pregnancy, but no child yet born.

Year 2 Days 82-109: The Shellbend fishers, still unidentified as a people, permitted Letha to watch from a respectful shore margin and voluntarily modeled the tidal mechanics of their stone weir with loose pebbles away from the working structure. Talumans showed fiber knots and gave one coil. No access rights, fishing permission, or binding agreement resulted; no work on their stone barrier.

Year 2 Day 94: Vessa and Arel finished a small, open-sided reed-roofed clay drying shelter and nearby outdoor pit-firing zone in Taluma, using local clay and materials. A subsequent nine-vessel test yielded five intact, including two with improved overnight water retention; practical small vessels only, not sealed storage or mass production.

Year 2 Day 116: Rema bore a daughter, Nala, in the existing high-dune household shared with Jorin. Seli and experienced caregivers assisted, and both are alive by Day 119. First recorded Taluman birth since founding; population now 68 with 73 housing capacity.

Year 2 Days 75-119: The Circle of Witnesses added the first pottery workshop and first birth to the community oral chronicle; Sora prepared a next-generation seed trial in dark mulched soil but no edible harvest credited. In cold storms Nemi lost one food-day of stored fish and council restored storage protections.

Year 2 Days 120-160: Nemi and Letha tested a modest removable loose-stone tidal guide with a woven basket trap inside Taluma lagoon, well away from inhabited Shellbend fishing grounds and normal domestic water collection. First high tide shifted its stones; a redesigned wider, low barrier held through ordinary tides. Additional preserved catch totaled about two settlement-day equivalents over the period. The experimental trap remains vulnerable to storm surge and cannot yet substitute for ordinary fishing.

Year 2 Days 127-153: Arel and Vessa located accessible workable clay and a modest stony outcrop above the tideline on the already used Taluman side of the southern headland, away from Shellbend and any marked inland route. Two stone loads were carried to Taluma; one used for the reversible local fish-trap prototype. Clay prospects are useful but extraction and firing are labor- and fuel-limited.

Year 2 Days 142-150: A voluntary daytime craft gathering in Taluma hosted one streamside inland potter and one Shellbend fisher, each free to depart and each remaining outside the other community's restricted grounds. The fisher modeled tide channels and shell weights; the inland guest showed tempering clay. Taluman hosts demonstrated cordage repair and dried-fish racks. The coastal and inland groups observed each other but no shared identity, formal alliance or durable agreement is inferred.

Year 2 Days 161-205: Nemi and Letha widened the Taluma-local reversible tidal experiment with a second removable woven creel, carefully avoiding the inhabited Shellbend barrier. Early winter surges scattered an unsecured basket, but lower-set stone guides and tie-points improved survival in ordinary tides. Together trials provided approximately 3 additional settlement-days of preserved food within routine production over 45 days; longer-term impacts on fish juveniles and weather remain unknown.

Year 2 Days 168-198: Arel and rotating adult haulers marked and improved the return route from the known unoccupied Taluma-side headland exposure. It safely carried 3 small stone loads and 3 fresh clay basketloads in usable weather; shifting tides still interrupt transit. Neither a cart road nor an unconstrained quarry exists.

Year 2 Days 174 and 199: Vessa hosted two optional, nonbinding daytime craft gatherings in Taluma for willing nearby residents. At least one Shellbend fisher attended one gathering; a familiar inland clay worker attended another. Guests were free to leave and no shared group identity, territorial rights, woodland entry or treaty were inferred.

Year 2 Day 182: With Seli overseeing safety and rest, Council formally began the Open Learning Days cycle, short supervised practical demonstrations for interested older children and young apprentices at regular moon gatherings. Activities include safe knots, clay shaping away from firing, seasonal field observations, tidal marks from land, and witnessed histories. No forced attendance, dangerous waterfront work, fire work, or assignment as adult labor.

Year 2 Days 192-205: an older child named Leni showed careful attention to the tide marks, observing that a steep basket could retain small juvenile fish. Nemi and Letha modified the Taluma test creel to allow hand-release of very small fish. Benefits and conservation effect remain unproven; the example is useful teaching, not a mature scientific breakthrough.

Year 2 Days 214-245: small western dune trickle gives temporary rain-season water; a shared groundwater source with the protected upper seep is possible. No independent or safe backup supply established.

Year 2 Day 274: One Taluman roof-fed rain catchment retained water for a few days after rainfall, while an additional western dune collector cracked and failed. Rainwater accumulated leaf and soil debris, so the successful collector is restricted to craft and cleaning use, not assumed safe for consumption. This may modestly reduce demand on fresh spring water for workshop tasks but is NOT an independent drinking-water supply.

Year 2 Day 281: Annual Meeting of Many Hands inaugurated at Taluma with voluntary participation of some inland and Shellbend neighbors. Distinct from smaller everyday Open Learning Days; no formal alliance or common language established.

Year 2 Days 301-332: Scouts led by Corun explored a western gravel shelf beyond the previously surveyed seasonal dune trickle, along an unmarked route with no signs of current occupation observed. About a half-day walk west of Taluma, a small running channel emerged beneath a rocky bank. Three observations, including one after 10 days with no significant rainfall, found moving water. No proof of year-round flow, microbiological safety or groundwater independence; this source is NOT yet used as potable settlement water and is not a Taluman territorial claim.

Year 2 Days 305-328: Letha, Vessa and other adult facilitators tested reciprocal, witnessed barter using paired pebble counts, displayed goods and separate gestures for acceptance or refusal. Two one-time voluntary exchanges occurred: at Shellbend outside the active fish-weir and with willing inland guests on the Taluma side of the ochre cord. No standardized currency, enforced contract, debt, treaty, woodland crossing, fishing rights or territorial claims established.

Year 2 Day 346: Corun, Tovan and two rotating adults began a nonintrusive assessment of Western Gravel Run ~half a day west. They found a gravel bench capable of temporary shelter but observed lodged branches well above the channel, suggesting occasional flood surges. No human use confirmed or denied. No posts set or ownership asserted.

Year 2 Days 351-365: after an extended drier interval, Western Gravel Run flow persisted but noticeably thinned. It is not independent groundwater verified, safe drinking-water tested, or adequate for a satellite settlement. A seasonal probe found surface moisture but could not justify residency or permanent water hauling.

Year 2 Day 353: Council opened a removable roofed trading ground beside the Hall of Many Hands on existing Taluman land. Visitors from Shellbend and inland communities were invited, not obliged. Goods inspected, counted with stones; no standard currency, tariff, price schedule or legal jurisdiction beyond voluntary Taluman hospitality.

Year 2 Day 362: Shellbend fisher refused a partly damp fish basket and withdrew without penalty. Nemi replaced the questionable basket with sound preserved fish at a later visit, demonstrating right of refusal and quality inspection; no binding deal was imposed.

Year 3 Day 2: after the village year changed, second successful voluntary trading day at Taluma, several nonbinding exchanges of prepared fish, cordage, small clay temper and worked shell tools, with visitors free to leave. No treaty, land concession, guaranteed future attendance or extended inland woodland access.

Year 3 Day 4: West survey recommendation: possible small future outpost area on upper gravel shelf but seasonal flow, potable safety, flood risk, winter access and neighbors unknown. Scout observations qualify it for continued tests, not founding. Nala of Rema and Jorin is roughly 8 months old and observed crawling; unchanged population 68.

Year 3 Days 10-31: Maro, Vessa and Nemi developed one Taluman reference basket for measuring specified dry goods by level fill, with pebble counting and visual inspection of dampness and quality. Visitors were free to choose the measure or negotiate a different one. An uneven shell-tool trade was voluntarily stopped and restarted when both sides clarified quantity; no currency, compulsory conversion or fixed price.

Year 3 Days 15-35: Corun and Letha surveyed alternative coastal and dune outpost candidates without crossing Shellbend fishing ground or the inland ochre line. The nearest ridge lacked independent fresh water; a sheltered raised northern bench, named Longbank Terrace by the scouts, looked less flood-exposed but still had unverified intermittent seep and wind. Western Gravel Bench remains unsuitable due to possible flooding and low flow. No place founded.

Year 3 Days 20-44: Vessa and Iren shaped fourteen small-lid and storage-pot experiments from local gathered clay. Eight survived drying and firing, three paired lids fit acceptably for sheltered dry-seed trials; a fourth vessel cracked during damp-weather cycling. The tests can protect small dry seed samples from splashes and some pests but do not prove food safety, watertightness, or storage for a full year. No bulk grain harvest exists. Firing uses an extra 3 settlement-fuel-days included in actual consumption.

Year 3 Day 42: Three willing settlers, Sena, Daro and their child Tiri, relocated from the Shellbend coastal group to an already available Taluman housing section by invitation after discussions of food and shared rules. No Shellbend trap access or land rights transferred. Population now 71; Taluma may request their knowledge but cannot require it. Their original friends and community remain independent.

Year 3 Days 56-82: Council-directed building crews added two small weatherproof high-dune family shelters, four places each, on existing Taluman ground. Wind anchoring, hearth clearance, routine repair stock and water-carry access were checked. Housing rose from 73 to 81; resources and flexible workforce were consumed, without a new outpost or claim.

Year 3 Days 63-96: Corun, Arel and helpers reorganized main upper-spring collection with raised vessel-rests, simple reed covers, regular cleaning, separate drinking-water deliveries, and controlled waiting queues. Twenty-three days of observed draw showed no persistent depletion under normal autumn conditions with present population; neither contamination-free potability nor safe additional population capacity through drought has been scientifically established. Unverified western seep, Longbank seep and rainwater continue excluded from drinking supply.

Year 3 Day 91: Tama, a willing adult reed-weaver, and Kelan, a willing adult stone-and-carry-frame worker from the inland stream community, elected to settle in newly available Taluma housing after multiple voluntary visits. They came to Taluma-side meeting place unescorted across the existing marked boundary, without Taluman entry into restricted woodland and without agreements obligating their original community. Both are Taluman residents by free choice; participation in projects remains voluntary.

Year 3 Days 65-103: Trade continues at optional reference-basket measure with witnessed inspection. A waterlogged basket of dry fiber was refused without conflict; a replacement basket was accepted on a different day. Pottery workshop suspended most kiln sessions until winter fuel rose; two modest test firings yielded three serviceable dry-seed lids, but no proof of durable all-weather storage. Sora kept experimental seedbeds and selected saved seed distinct from protected emergency reserves.

Year 3 Day 290: Two specifically permitted neighboring shelter-study visits exchanged practical techniques: Shellbend Day 249 and an escorted inland village visit Day 272. No unrestricted crossing, rights, treaty or settlement expansion followed.

Year 3 Day 290: A dry-weather 12-day sample of Taluma upper spring produced approximately 86-94 standardized daily per-person water shares at the draw point, with an observed low of 86. At 73 resident-average shares daily, 100 residents would require about 100; observed spring yield ALONE does not support declaring capacity for 100, especially with unobserved true drought or seasonal deterioration. Water shares are a rough local comparison unit, not known liters or proof of pathogen-free water.

GEOGRAPHIC CANON Year13 Day302: Historical discovery chronicle has Shellbend Cove SOUTH of Taluma (Year1 southern headland), Reedmouth Inlet NORTH beyond Longbank (Year4); Crescent Shoal and Ternhook farther north, unknown coast beyond Ternhook. Any later narration/map placing Shellbend north or as a stop on a northern trip is a continuity error, not a changed coastline. Southern exploration beyond Shellbend toward Windcut Bay is first recorded Year13 Days252-270. Distances and exact coordinates remain estimates, not surveyed facts.

Year14 Day19 observed atlas update: SOUTH of Taluma: Shellbend Cove, Windcut Bay, White-Reed Point farther south (last offshore observed frontier). NORTH: Reedmouth Inlet, Crescent Shoal, Ternhook Inlet, Northreach Estuary farther north (seaward channel observed, source not surveyed). Interior Upper Path/Splitstone/Farbank green stone region approximate. No map scale or inferred permanent territorial claims.
setting.fog_of_war: Known Taluma lagoon, dunes and north-dune seep; permitted local woodland fringe; northwestern ochre-cord woodland and stony stream still closed without consent; beyond the southern headland, Shellbend Cove contains an actively maintained fish-weir and coastal people with whom Letha has had one peaceful face-to-face gift exchange. Their homes, name and political identity remain unknown; no cove harvesting or land claim. Wider coast and inland remain unexplored. Year 2 Day 160: Taluma-local lagoon contains one small removable experimental tidal trap; a previously unoccupied Taluman-side headland outcrop supplies limited stone and clay. Neither new coastal nor inland territory claimed; Shellbend fishery work area and ochre cord remain restricted. Year 2 Day 205: the only increased lagoon trap work occurred inside Taluma tidal waters; new small clay/stone loads from previously mapped Taluma-side headland, with a marked return route. Neighbor fisheries and ochre-marked inland lands remain restricted. Year 2 Day 246: Western dune trickle surveyed within Taluma’s ordinary use area, apparently seasonal and not yet independent of principal spring. No further territory surveyed or claimed. Year 2 Day 333: Western Gravel Run mapped approximately a half-day west of Taluma, beyond the unreliable western dune trickle. Surface flow seen three times including during a dry spell. Wider watershed and local inhabitants remain unknown; no territorial claim and no potable use. Contact with Shellbend and inland people remains voluntary and strictly outside their restricted areas. Year 4 Day 47: water reconnaissance extended past Longbank on accessible ground short of the protected ochre-cord woodland. Northfold Seep seen flowing in a separate visible channel but aquifer independence, drinking quality, previous users and lasting flow unknown. No claim, extraction or outpost. Year4 Days356-Year5 Day10: exploratory paired adults followed the permitted near-coast route past Reedmouth meeting beach but stopped at tide-cut shoals. Distant smoke beyond North Shoals Outer Point is a potential human-activity clue, but source could be Reedmouth-associated people or something else; no new people discovered or access permission inferred. Paused independent fresh-water scouting not resumed. Year5 Days23-45: Reedmouth fishers on neutral shore indicated that some families and work groups follow seasonal fish movement to outer shoal drying sites, explaining recent smoke; not proof of a new people. Taluman paired scouts and a consenting Reedmouth guide watched from safe side, never crossed risky tidal cut. Year5 Days31-54: reauthorized non-extractive Northfold observations after spring flow narrowed to79 shares for74 residents; seep still flows after moderate dryness, but new human footprints advise obtaining site-user consent before approaching farther or extracting. No other reliable water supply qualified. Year5 Days69-129: Letha and Corun traced Northfold footmarks to two adult seasonal water-stop users connected through Reedmouth itinerant fishers; two limited host-accepted observational site visits, no extraction, no residency, no rights. One rain-catch expansion supports only seasonal nonpotable and tightly supervised promptly used boil batches. Reedmouth seasonal knowledge-exchange introductions now repeated on consent, but neither side pledged perpetual attendance or territory permissions. Year5 Days130-194: limited hosted Northfold observations over roughly six weeks exposed variation and possible serious warm-season decline, still no drinkable-source qualification; joint Hall craftspeople from three neighbors attended freely. No further uninvited shoreline or woodland travel, no new territories. Year9 Day207: the Upper Path route to Splitstone Rest was opened for one hosted exchange; two Farbank travelers are known through it, but their lands and trade source routes are unmapped/unconsented. The distant greenish stone remains unexplained.

known_locations.name: Taluma
known_locations.description: New camp on a sandy rise above a tidal lagoon
known_locations.status: controlled

known_locations.name: North dune seep
known_locations.description: Only verified freshwater supply, now suspected of salinity
known_locations.status: known

known_locations.name: Near tidal flats
known_locations.description: Observed shellfish and fishing grounds
known_locations.status: known

known_locations.name: Upper seep trickle
known_locations.description: Narrow upslope trickle consistently fresh to taste in observed tide cycles; rudimentary raised draw point and diversion groove constructed. Currently yields enough collected water with scheduled trips for existing settlement, but output in drought/winter and microbial safety unverified.
known_locations.status: protected collection point; seasonally unverified

known_locations.name: Rooted dune bench
known_locations.description: A higher, sheltered bench north-northeast of Taluma; root-bound sand with two occupied six-person shelters, accessed by a marked water-carrying path. Winter suitability still untested.
known_locations.status: surveyed; occupied with two six-person shelters; water carried

known_locations.name: Shifting dune saddle
known_locations.description: Loose sand with little shelter; not recommended for construction
known_locations.status: surveyed; unoccupied

known_locations.name: Northwest gravel rise
known_locations.description: Firm but uneven rise beyond the near scrubwood fringe, reached by the first seven-day inland reconnaissance. Marked narrow foot route; heavy carrying difficult over intervening dunes. Some difficult sections of the old markers were lightly cleared Days 56-65; relay hauling tested but reliable transport not yet achieved.
known_locations.status: partial marked footpath; no claim

known_locations.name: Inland wooded swale
known_locations.description: Small sheltered woodland basin about one day outward walk from Taluma in fair weather, with saplings, mature mixed trees and scattered deadwood. Potential longer-term gathering area, unproven yield and hauling cost. Weathered tool-like scars on one fallen trunk; source unknown. Follow-up survey found struck stone flakes near an earlier weathered marked trunk; likely old woodworking, date and origin unidentified. One small trial relay brought home a drywood sample.
known_locations.status: Visited but ochre-corded inland route remains off-limits to Taluman timber gatherers; Day 224 gesture suggests crossing is unwelcome; no formal territorial claim confirmed.

known_locations.name: Stony inland stream
known_locations.description: Small stream beyond northwest wooded swale, reached after an additional inland traverse. Water persistence, drinking safety and accessibility with supplies untested. Small cold-ash and stone setting and an indistinct possible footprint nearby suggest possible past or recent visitors, but no people seen. On follow-up, three short morning flow checks found continuous shallow moving water; later seasonal flow/potability unknown. Two unknown people seen on opposite bank, neither approached nor identified; no claim or treaty.
known_locations.status: reconnoitered twice; unidentified people sighted; unclaimed and not a supply site

known_locations.name: Shellbend Cove
known_locations.description: Sheltered inlet beyond southern headland with worked stone tidal fish weir, good shellfish habitat and apparently useful clay seams. Year 2 Days 43-57: Letha and two Taluman companions respectfully introduced themselves from outside the active weir. At first the fishers stopped their approach; later an adult fisher agreed to a small, nonbinding exchange of one coil of Taluman cordage for a worked shell scraper. The visiting party never crossed the fishing installation or touched any stones. An adult fisher and a younger companion maintained the weir throughout. No village, group name, connection to inland people or resource access rights established.
known_locations.status: Active fishing site of unidentified coastal people; peaceful first contact and single small reciprocal gift; no ongoing rights, ownership, or harvest permission.

known_locations.name: Taluma lagoon trial trap
known_locations.description: Small removable low-tide fish guide and woven basket situated within the already inhabited Taluma lagoon; repaired after an initial surge; yields modest extra catch
known_locations.status: Taluman trial site, not permanent weir

known_locations.name: Taluma-side headland clay and stone exposure
known_locations.description: Accessible clay and limited loose stone above the tide line on already traversed shore outside the occupied Shellbend work area; extraction is labor-intensive
known_locations.status: surveyed local resource site; no new land claim

known_locations.name: Western dune seasonal trickle
known_locations.description: Small wet hollow west of the Taluma dune village, observed after rains. Only four observations in spring; fresh tasting but slow, fading in dry spell. May share subsurface water with existing north-dune seep. Surface collection liner leaks.
known_locations.status: surveyed; possible supplemental rainy-season water, NOT proven backup or potable source

known_locations.name: Western Gravel Run
known_locations.description: A small moving channel beneath a rocky shelf around a half-day west of Taluma on an exploratory route beyond the seasonal dune trickle. Seen flowing on three visits including after about ten dry days; little evidence of active human use was seen, but no ownership or isolation from the coastal groundwater is proven. Water has not been made safe or accepted for drinking. Carrying water to Taluma would be labor-intensive.
known_locations.status: Newly surveyed; candidate independent seasonal fallback, flow and safety unverified; no claim, no supply infrastructure

known_locations.name: Western Gravel Bench (candidate only)
known_locations.description: High gravel shelf near Western Gravel Run, roughly half a day west of Taluma on surveyed return route. Apparent space for a handful of shelters, but seasonal water inadequate/unverified and high drift debris warns of flood pulses. No structure, territorial claim, permanent residents or proven potable supply.
known_locations.status: Reconnaissance only; outpost not authorized or founded; no confirmed neighboring presence or absence.

known_locations.name: Longbank Terrace (survey candidate only)
known_locations.location_type: unoccupied status unconfirmed, exploratory alternative to Western Gravel Bench
known_locations.description: Raised northern coastal bench reached along mapped Taluma-side dunes, away from Shellbend Cove and the inland ochre boundary. Two scouting visits found firmer rooted ground, no obvious recent flood debris, a small seep and wind-exposed passages. The seep has NOT been observed through drought, tested for safe water or shown independent of the main spring. No proof that others never use it.
known_locations.status: Feasibility scouting only; no camp, outpost, water diversion, occupation or territorial claim.

known_locations.name: Northfold Seep (survey candidate only)
known_locations.description: Narrow flow from stony north-facing slope beyond Longbank Terrace reached by an accessible non-ochre survey route. Different visible surface runnel from Taluma upper spring, with two dated observations including after ~11 dry days; no proof of separate groundwater, full-season flow, drinking suitability, daily carrying practicality, prior-use status or water rights. No extraction, residence or permanent structure. Year5 Days31 and54: Corun returned by known permissible nonintrusive path after renewed player authorization; flow continued after about14 comparatively dry days; counted volume not shown sufficient for whole community. Signs of recent human footprints nearby, so usage and permission must be clarified before sampling, diversion or occupation. Year5 Days80-119: Taluma respectfully identified two periodic reed-path users associated with Reedmouth travelers; these individuals agreed to two escorted observations of the seep-bank from the public-looking approach, without drinking-water sampling, bank modification or extraction. Observed winter seep ongoing. Host demonstration suggests warmer-season decline, exact meaning uncertain and no year-round safe yield established. Year5 Days149-190: four escorted non-extractive daytime observations by Corun and Letha under a separately renewed permission series from two seasonal users. Winter/late-winter flow remained visible but lowered notably during a relatively dry spell. Hosts signaled possible very low warm-season flow; uncertain shared language. No verified full-season reliable or drinkable supply, no diversion, building, claim or guaranteed future access. Year5 Day302: with fresh, single-visit host consent arranged only for a warm-season observation, Corun/Letha found continuous surface run nearly absent: a few damp gravel pockets and tiny intermittent trickles, far below winter flow. No extraction or sample, no markers left and no further visit permission. This is insufficient as an independently dependable water source for target100; user instructed NOT to push Northfold beyond this warm-season observation.
known_locations.status: Year5 Day320: warm-season one-time observation complete and permission expired. Seasonal flow essentially collapsed. Northfold is removed from Taluma growth-water development queue and will NOT be pursued, sampled, negotiated, built on, diverted or revisited unless the guiding intelligence explicitly reopens it.

known_locations.name: Reedmouth Inlet (provisional Taluman name)

known_locations.description: Narrow reed-edged northern tidal inlet beyond Longbank Terrace on a walkable coast route, distinct from Shellbend Cove and inland ochre woods. Scouting Year4 Day271 revealed seasonal woven-shade camp and float-lines for a net. Three adults encountered at a respectful open-sand margin on Days282 and 298; small one-off trade made. Unfamiliar community name and home location not yet understood.

known_locations.name: North Shoals Outer Point (provisional Taluman description)

known_locations.description: During Year4 Day356 coastal learning walk, adult scouts at the safe near-shore side of a tide-cut headland observed smoke beyond distant northern shoals and scattered older reed float remnants. Source and users uncertain; not visited, no evidence yet of a distinct people. Route can close quickly at rising tide. Year5 Day38 Reedmouth guest demonstrated shifting seasonal fish-drying activity near/behind shoals; Year5 Day45 a host-approved joint watch from safe approach linked recent smoke to Reedmouth seasonal work. No distinct fourth group confirmed. Tide access remains dangerous.
known_locations.status: Distant smoke most plausibly Reedmouth seasonal processing fires by direct consented guide demonstration; no crossing or permanent access. More distant coasts remain unseen.

known_locations.name: Upper Path Gravel Shelf (provisional Taluman description)
known_locations.location_type: temporarily hosted inland observation place, specific Upper Path-used ridge route
known_locations.description: First consented guided inland day stop above non-ochre gravel ridge. Pebble and gravel deposits over compact gray clay, intermittent runoff rills and some fine dark stone bands. Green polished stone travels along exchange hands but original quarry remains unknown. No proof of a new groundwater source, no public road access.
known_locations.status: Year7 Days308-319: scouts visited once with Upper Path guide and two relevant hosts permission for exact segment. No water withdrawal, stone extraction, unauthorized travel or new territorial claim. Further trip requires fresh consent.

civilization.name: Taluma
civilization.government: Council of the Shore (seven seasonally reviewed representatives: Esha, Nemi, Corun, Arel, Seli, Vessa and Maro; permanent essential-services mandate)
delegated_powers: organize and allocate routine labor to fishing, shellfish, water collection, firewood, and caregiving
manage food drying, smoking, and preservation practices using available tools
maintain fresh water access and take immediate reversible safety precautions
repair existing shelters and authorize small low-risk shelter additions using ordinary stores
maintain seed protection and plan routine seasonal supplies
respond to immediate threats to life and report major decisions to the guiding intelligence
represent households through seven council members, with seasonal review of seats

PERMANENT: autonomously reserve sufficient baseline labor, including relief and substitute crews, for daily food gathering/preservation, drinking-water collection/protection, shelter inspection/repair, firewood replacement, and essential caregiving without waiting for repeat guidance.

PERMANENT: measure food and wood against at least 30 days of settlement consumption, reassign flexible labor promptly if either drops below the minimum; prioritize safe drinking water and habitable shelter first in emergencies, then minimum food and fuel.

PERMANENT: maintain schedules, inventory records, seasonal inspections and work rotations; use only approved low-risk routine resources and report shortages, exhaustion, environmental decline or conflicts to the guiding intelligence.

Limit: the permanent labor mandate does not authorize coercive universal labor, consumption of protected seeds, major migration, land claims, irreversible ecological damage, treaties, wars or significant constitutional change.

Year 3 Day 4 PLAYER DIRECTIVE: encourage voluntary family growth through maternal/infant care and practical housing preparation, and actively invite individual settlers and households who want to join Taluma and contribute. Council may welcome a small freely choosing household within current unused safe housing and water capacity; do not undertake major migration, forced relocation, coercive reproduction, or settlement founding without player approval.

cultural_institutions: The Rain Hands: every Taluman household contributes a safe, capacity-appropriate task to seasonal common rain-catching and vessel stewardship. Roles include screens and gutters, tally/witness records, fitting lids, nonpotable hauling, caring for dependents while others work, and organizing supplies. Council makes accommodations for illness, disability, infancy and caregiving; essential spring access is not conditional on work. Adopted Year6 Day111, first common maintenance day Year6 Day132.

Year6 Day236: Sora, Maro and the households inaugurated the paired seasonal Day of the First Furrow (soil/seed preparation, early in workable season) and Gathering of Seed Heads (witnessed small harvest, seed selection and teachers thanked). Voluntary teaching custom, no land expansion or compulsory labor. Mature new field produced 3 settlement-food-day equivalents, not a staple.

Year7 Day77: The Hall of Many Hands continues witnessed, voluntary teaching exchanges with Reedmouth, Shellbend and inland guests, including supervised visiting children and carers, with teacher/source credit, no compulsory attendance, no permanent permissions. The Shore Walks continue as adult coastal scouting trips with tides, return points and no crossing protected or closed areas.

Year7 Day151: annual Gathering of Seed Heads and Day of the First Furrow remain observed by Sora and Maro with voluntary apprentices and teacher attribution; grain source plots and selected descendants identified by oral witness and pictographs. New Shore Walk meeting at consented Reedmouth neutral beach and voluntary Hall education continue across communities, without territorial rights.

Year7 Day274: recurring Hall learning exchange hosted under fresh separate invitations; Reedmouth fisher and Upper Path stoneworker demonstrated no-iron stone shaping and cord bindings, with clear teacher attribution. Inland visiting children remain only with consenting caregivers. Shore Walks and local upland observation walks maintain separate safety roles.

Year7 Day331: first full household-by-household resident census (18 hearth groups,77 verified people) with witnessed family records and a correction for child whose care ties spanned two hearths; visitors not counted. Repeat yearly and after material population change, protecting private family and care information. Shore Walks and voluntary visits remain scheduled.

Year8 Days35-38: Hall of Many Hands hosted two willing Upper Path craft teachers under reciprocal invitation with host-site consent, supervised stone-flaking and cord-bound handle instruction, recognized teachers in oral/witness archives; no migration or treaty. Day47 Rain Hands and Maro water-register check for clean 48-hour spring-water jar rotation; not long-term safe supply.

Established freshwater security service (Year10 Day304 accounting reconciliation): Rain Hands and Seli/Corun run routine short-batch rainwater treatment and clean distribution; at historic spring low, existing covered raw storage supports a modeled 21-day shortage without requiring a new source. No time advanced for the rule correction.

Year11 Day12: first recurring-season Taluma shore market hosted by prior invitation with Reedmouth, Shellbend and Upper Path; Maro/Leni record trade proposals and provenance and Nemi witnesses weights and quality; no permanent treaty or nonresident automatic access.

Year11 Day68: second invitation-based Taluma shore market welcomed consented Crescent Shoal, Reedmouth and Shellbend visitors; explicit hosted invitations and inspection, no automatic landing/harbor/fishing rights, voluntary craft exchanges, household records by Maro and Leni.

Year11 Days134-180: the invited Shore Market Rhythm organized by Nemi, Sena, Maro and visiting partners. Two potential exchange windows per year near favorable tide and fishing rhythms; Taluma sends and receives confirmations for each session and participants inspect goods. The first gathering under the rhythm held on Day180 with Crescent Shoal, Reedmouth, Shellbend; no universal landing rights, binding price guarantees, taxation or permanent outside trading claim.

Year11 Day209: Daro/Vessa green-stone ornament teaching bench at Hall of Many Hands, two supervised adolescent or adult apprentices plus safe polishing instruction using ordinary stones before limited green stone; recorded labor and conservation of specimens. Not a new permanent building or mandated child labor.

Year11 Day232: revised invitation-only Shore Market with temporary shade-stalls, separate inspected provisions and marked exchange tablets by Nemi/Maro/Leni, and a designated public landing window confirmed by Reedmouth, Shellbend, Crescent Shoal and one accompanied Upper Path guest. No automatic foreign landing or fisheries rights.

Year11 Days277-365 / Year12 Days1-9: Witnessing of Hearths: optional adult-to-adult public partnership acknowledgement, with both partners affirming agreement, mutual care and the freedom to decline; Kiva and Ralen first participants. No arranged or child marriage, compulsory pairing, pregnancy targets for individuals, or unequal access to supplies.

Year11 Days277-365 / Year12 Days1-9: Family Welcome and Apprenticeship Circle: Seli coordinates prenatal and postpartum help, Nemi allocates family food, Arel maintains safe new sleeping places, Maro registers consenting adult household commitments, and the Council welcomes skilled applicants after agreement on work and residence. Long-term Growing Shore plan target of roughly110-120 residents by Year16 contingent on ordinary supplies, housing and voluntary choices; not automatic population growth.

Year11 Days277-365 / Year12 Days1-9: Dedicated Taluma Boatyard: Hadan and Tira run supervised practical boat-construction and repair teaching at dry raised shore rack with sheltered fittings and replaceable ribs. Permanent separate invitation-based annual market dates proposed, each participating partner confirming separately.

Year12 Days10-97 (88 days): Growing Shore new residential bench: two five-place, storm-protected family houses completed from existing reserved supplies on existing Taluman tenure, community footpath/drainage assessed; two replacement home kits earmarked from remaining material totals, maternal care and 90-day food floor independent. Two incoming skilled families joined by consent, active midwifery and apprenticeship system continues without coercive quotas.

Year12 Days10-97 (88 days): Shore Pilots Circle supervised by Letha, Hadan, Seren and visiting Crescent Shoal guide. Two local trainee pilots learn tide-mark recognition, coastal bearings, weather turn-back protocols, signaling, and load trim. Long-range exploration charter drafted for Year13; NOT launched ahead of year boundary.

Year12 Day142: Growing Shore welcome-and-care review: voluntary immigration evaluated for housing, child care, food, actual teacher and craft opportunity; welcome skilled or contributing applicants where support available, no arbitrary growth quota or forced marriage/birth; a visiting candidate can be hosted and assisted while deciding.

Year12 Day272: Council family-care and apprenticeship roster: Seli and Nemi coordinate relief for pregnant/recovering caregivers, infants and elders; Maro audits household requests privately, adults freely choose partnerships and children; three adult trainees receive supervised coastal and craft skills without losing essential worker coverage.

Year13 Day47: Shore Pilot Circle formalized a repeatable tide/landmark/abort record used on first long-range expedition; voyage reports clearly distinguish witnessed facts from tentative interpretation.

Year13 Day104: Shore Households Circle formalized a confidential and voluntary family, newborn, elder-care and apprenticeship scheduling review. Seli/Nemi assign relief based on expressed household need, Maro verifies fair distribution without publicly exposing private conditions; children in safe teaching, no compelled partner or childbearing.

Year13 Day115: Pilot and Boatwright School continues under Letha, Hadan and Tira with paired pupil responsibilities: launch checks, cargo shifting, tidal observations, repair bundles and explicit turnback tests; apprentice achievement recorded separately from full open-coast qualification.

Year13 Day216: Leni recognized as a fully responsible adult archive instructor after more than a decade as voluntary child apprentice; witnessed census moves one resident from children to adults, and Maro remains senior mentor. No new resident created.

Year13 Days135-227: Shore Households Circle guarantees consenting adult craft trainees protected learning shifts with essential-work substitutes; Seli/Nemi honor requested postpartum and elder help, private fairness checks, self-directed family choices; no compulsory pairings or demographic targets.

Year13 Day211: Ternhook and Taluma developed a tentative two-window seasonal invitation exchange rhythm, subject to confirmation and the approval of local hosts each visit; no bilateral treaty or automatic landing/fishing rights.

Year13 Day302: Leni began a two-learner coast-and-route record course, reconciling Shellbend SOUTH, Reedmouth NORTH and the relative coastal journeys. Records mark uncertain locations as observations, not measured absolute positions. Boat crews and council consult this register to avoid route confusion.

Year14 Day19: The Hall of Many Hands maintains the Three-Hide Coastal Atlas. Maro and adult instructor Leni reconciled two voyage logs against the home master hide; two boat-ready northern and southern hide sheets use charcoal, red earth and notches for landmark order, tidal hazards and uncertainty. No claim to absolute distances or uncontacted shore rights. Apprentices copy only confirmed observations and retain clay/wood record backups.

Year14 Day77: Shore Pathfinders Circle, volunteer adult training in coastline/inland navigation, mapping and respectful diplomacy led by Tovan, Rela, Kelan, Letha; one Upper Path adult Ilan settled to help path training.
Year14 Day99: Shore Words, a preliminary cross-community vocabulary project with 18 trade meanings; speakers verify before treating a term as shared, long-term institution.

Year14 Day183: The Shore Words circle teaches a carefully checked 34-meaning intercommunity trade glossary (not a shared fluent language); the volunteer Shore Pathfinders have completed one host-guided inland survey and archive all maps as observation, report or hypothesis.

Year14 Day260: Shore Watch and Welcome Signals, an eight-adult rotating watch/training roster with dune lookouts, shell-call alerts, protected stores, practiced voluntary household shelter instructions, contact-first de-escalation and rescue roles. Year14 Day260: Shore Words teaching group reaches 49 mutually checked practical meanings across trade and safety demonstrations, five disputed forms remain unverified; no fluent intercommunity language established.

resources.accounting_basis:
All food and wood-fuel days are at current 67-person consumption rates; protected seeds excluded from edible food stores. Water availability depends on spring safety and daily collection. First work period (6 days): food 19 - 6 consumed + 5 gathered and preserved = 18; fuel 13 - 6 burned + 12 gathered = 19. Building pole and reed gains are separate from fuelwood, and no protected seed was consumed. Second period (8 days): food 18 - 8 consumed + 13 gathered/preserved = 23; fuel 19 - 8 burned + 9 gathered = 20. Higher-dune six-person shelter cost 6 poles, 12 reed bundles, 1 stone load and 1 cordage coil; seeds untouched. Twelve project adults: 4 on augmented fisheries/preservation, 5 on high-dune shelter, 3 on gathering fuel; ongoing 24 essential workers maintained routine duties. Third period (10 days, Days 16-25): food 23 - 10 consumed + 15 caught/gathered/preserved = 28; wood fuel 20 - 10 burned + 15 gathered = 25. Project allocations first 5 days: 4 shelter, 3 food, 3 fuel, 2 spring; last 5 days: 4 shelter, 3 food, 5 fuel. Second six-person shelter cost 6 poles, 12 reeds, 1 stone load, 1 cordage coil; spring headworks cost 2 reed bundles and 1 stone load. Protected seed unchanged. Fourth period (10 days, Days 26-35): project workers first five days 5 fuel, 3 reeds, 3 storm protection, 1 food; second five days 8 fuel, 3 reeds, 1 food. 24 routine essential workers continued regular activities. Food 28 - 10 consumed + 11 preserved = 29. Heating fuel 25 - 10 burned + 16 gathered = 31, clearing 30-day target (but maintenance remains necessary). Reeds 9 + 15 gathered - 7 repairs = 17; poles 11 - 4 = 7, stone loads 6 - 1 = 5, cordage 2 - 1 = 1. Protection strengthened both high-dune shelters and three older weak roofs, drainage channels cleared; one minor roof seam leak during Day 31 squall patched. Upper water draw point observed/maintained through normal routines. Seed protected, 2 food-day equivalents untouched. Fresh reed bundles are partly still curing; do not treat all as immediately dry for major roof building. Fifth period (10 days, Days 36-45): Council autonomously assigned 12 project adults: 4 to additional fish/shellfish preservation, 5 to longer-range deadwood collection, 2 to plant-fiber cordage production, and 1 to spring/catchment inspection and roof/drain upkeep; 24 routine essential workers continued baseline support, 4 adults unfit for heavy work. Food 29 - 10 consumed + 14 gathered/preserved = 33 days. Fuel 31 - 10 burned + 10 brought in = 31 days. Fiberwork used 2 older cured reed/rush bundles, resulting in 2 additional cordage coils: reeds 17 - 2 = 15, cordage 1 + 2 = 3. Poles 7, stones 5 unchanged. Two high-dune shelters still occupy 12 people and rely on carried water, no expansion. Protected seed untouched. Both 30-day targets maintained, but inland deadwood trips are longer, and storm-season spring performance remains uncertain. Sixth period (10 days, Days 46-55): four adults led by Tovan scouted inland for seven days, then joined the regular fuelwood crew for the last three days. First seven days: 4 scouts, 4 additional food/preservation, 3 fuel, 1 spring and roof routine inspection. Last three days: 4 food, 7 fuel, 1 inspection. No tools or goods consumed as build costs; scouting rations count within the ten settlement-days of baseline food consumption. Food 33 - 10 eaten + 12 preserved = 35. Fuel 31 - 10 burned + 8 gathered on increasingly long existing routes = 29; below council’s standing 30-day minimum. research_in_progress.name: Northfold seasonal negotiated shared use and distance logistics

research_in_progress.name: Trade and food surplus exchange network

research_in_progress.name: Short gravity-fed covered fresh-water transfer
research_in_progress.stage: Year9 Day282: 18-pace removable sloped trough from existing stand to lower experimental platform reduced nonpotable test leakage after repair, but a lid gap allowed debris. No tap on spring, no potable approval; most houses uphill.

research_in_progress.name: Dry-spell spring-output / water allocation audit
research_in_progress.stage: Year9 Day261 new observed spring low70 vs population77, Day263 infant Dena makes78. Handling losses about2 so only68 nominal household shares; drought emergency measures and differentiated caregiving activated before rain Day271.

research_in_progress.name: Consent-first Farbank trade expansion
research_in_progress.stage: Year9 Day236 hosted second meeting yielded finished trades of7 food days for2 stone loads and1 cordage coil plus craft knowledge; no access beyond meeting, green stone origin still unknown.

research_in_progress.name: Enclosed low-fired ceramic conduits for clean, gravity-assisted distribution
research_in_progress.stage: Year10 Day48: 12-pace 6-sleeve removable nonpotable prototype, comparable 24-jug runs delivered20 then23 after better collars; water film and cracked terminal sleeve require disassembly, sanitation testing and repair. NOT safe drinking distribution; no spring connection or uphill supply.

research_in_progress.name: Green stone provenance and inland river geology

Strong regional parent-rock candidate but no mineral ID, proven origin of original artifact, or access/quarrying rights.

research_in_progress.name: Local drinking water carrying capacity and emergency resilience
research_in_progress.stage: Year9 Day347: seasonal spring historical source low70 vs78 residents, approx2 delivery shares lost in severe dry conditions, no second validated supply. Shellbend conditional refuge4 for3 nights, Northfold open but hosts do not commit bulk dry-season water.

research_in_progress.name: Cleanable sealed-ceramic gravity conduits
research_in_progress.stage: Year10 Days74-138: eight accessible ceramic sleeves across18 paces; 32-jug comparisons delivered29 then31. Opening, cleaning and drying required ~1 adult working-day per complete cleanout; seam residue persisted after3 stagnant days. Nonpotable only, no connection to spring or household supply. Scaling and upkeep uncertain.

research_in_progress.name: Farbank green-stone craft and trade exchange
research_in_progress.stage: Year10 Day117: negotiated single completed witnessed barter of three already loose Farbank-controlled green stones for five settlement-food-days preserved fish. A separate proposed follow-up at next suitable host-invited seasonal meeting is conditional, not guaranteed. No quarrying, bedrock removal or ownership, mineral unconfirmed.

research_in_progress.name: Green-stone ornamental craft and material wear
research_in_progress.stage: Year10 Days163-212: Daro and Vessa spent about 12 distributed adult craft-days smoothing one of three legal Farbank pebbles by wet abrasive rubbing, wrapping a removable cord sleeve into a small wearable green ornament. One worked of six known samples; scratched surface and unknown mineral hardness; no sales/valuation proven.

research_in_progress.name: Operational serviceability of removable nonpotable ceramic conduit
research_in_progress.stage: Year10 Days158-219: improved joint support, paired end cleanouts and reed-fiber pull-through swab on 18-pace eight-section line; three 24-jug batches delivered23,23,22; ill-fitted joint led to last loss, repaired. Prompt draining and opening reduced full cleanout labor from1 to ~0.4 adult working-day, but 3-day standing water still develops residue. Supervised nonpotable workshop only.

research_in_progress.name: Housing capacity and full population census before expansion
research_in_progress.stage: Year10 Day190 counted 79 residents in18 hearth groups, Year10 Day205 expanded a preexisting weatherproof shelter by two ventilated berths (81->83), using unreserved repair materials only. No additional drinking source, further permanent influx still constrained by historic spring low70 daily shares.

research_in_progress.name: Demand and durability of crafted green stone pendants
research_in_progress.stage: Year10 Days263-274: invited visiting traders gave one declined offer, one one-coil offer, and one accepted Shellbend offer (two stone loads and two cordage coils) for single finished pendant, which was sold. Five unworked known-origin samples retained. Daro and Vessa still require ~12 adult-day craft cost, repeat demand unproven.

research_in_progress.name: Reliable potable source strategy and reversible spring collection
research_in_progress.stage: Year10 Days253-287: downstream spring clean-fill platform lowered measured loss from ~2 to~1 share per day; six dry days observed average73 source and~72 delivered against79 residents, with historic low70. Northfold observation with consent Year10 Day277 found seasonally weak flow; zero new dependable source or drinking network. Continue protective observation and request-specific neighboring help.

research_in_progress.name: Taluma coastal craft safety and maintainable lashings
research_in_progress.stage: Year11 Days38-57 Hadan/Tira/Arel built a buoyant two-person inshore reed craft using three wood poles, seven reed bundles and two cordage coils, acquired shell-bone fittings; supervised protected-inlet launch with two adults, rocked in crosswind, restored safely, not certified for open coast.

research_in_progress.name: Crescent Shoal tidal travel and coastal navigation
research_in_progress.stage: Year11 Days80-91 six Taluman adults plus two Shellbend host-guides visited the north coast through explicit permissions in two proven host boats; learned not to cross narrow cut at ebb, observed elevated boat racks and marked safe landing. No fisheries, permanent harbor rights or automatically recurring access.

research_in_progress.name: Safer three-person coast boat and tide-aware seamanship
research_in_progress.stage: Year11 Days133-178 new broad-beam craft with replaceable reed-bound braces, raised ends and transverse stability straps. Day166 three-person sheltered-inlet test under moderate lateral breeze stayed upright; Day178 shortened host-permitted coast-side day test aborted promptly when wind strengthened, all returned. Longer exposed trips/tidal-cut routes not yet authorized or proven; safety priority outranks distance.

research_in_progress.name: Green-stone ornament-making economy
research_in_progress.stage: Year11 Day180 Crescent Shoal guest voluntarily traded two sets of shell-bone boat fittings and one curved boat brace for previously unsold Taluman green pendant. Daro subsequently used ONE of nine then-unworked green pieces to produce a replacement cord-mounted pendant over eight adult working-days. 8 unworked, 1 finished retained, 2 historical pendants sold; mineral identity unknown, no guaranteed demand.

research_in_progress.name: Independent coastal cargo boats and weather judgment
research_in_progress.stage: Year11 Days215-257 lighter cargo lashings and inspection improved second Taluman three-person boat. First guided-by-own-crew (Hadan/Letha) limited Shellbend trip Days251-257 finished, with destination hosts consenting to landing; held one day for unfavorable wind. Longer journeys to Crescent Shoal remain future goal.

research_in_progress.name: Workshop training and market testing for green ornaments
research_in_progress.stage: Year11 Days208-276 Daro and Vessa started two-apprentice supervised green-stone bench; two finished new cord-mounted ornaments from two of eight original unworked stones, one original finished ornament exchanged on maiden voyage, ending6 unworked+2 finished. About7-8 adult-equivalent days per new pendant under supervision, small sample; demand varies by community.

research_in_progress.name: Larger Taluman cargo boat for open coastal passages
research_in_progress.stage: Year12 Day9: new 4-person rated wider craft demonstrated sheltered lagoon launch/cargo balance, needs weather/rate-of-load, tide cut and repair tests before use offshore; existing 3-person trained crew boat used with invited pilot to Crescent Shoal.

research_in_progress.name: Green-stone craft school and selective Farbank raw material procurement
research_in_progress.stage: Year12 Day9: 4 voluntary learners, 3 pendants produced this turn, two traded, seven unworked and three finished retained; prices vary and no quarry rights exist.

research_in_progress.name: Long-range northern-coast expedition preparations for Year13
research_in_progress.stage: Year12 Day97: LONG-RANGE VOYAGE NOT LAUNCHED. Explore beyond currently visited Crescent Shoal coast only after host-consented route, competent pilots, proven second boat and seaworthy cargo/provision capacity, weather, departure/turnback rules. Proposed Year13 seasonal window, not calendar guarantee.

research_in_progress.name: Crescent tide pilots and larger cargo boat
research_in_progress.stage: Two resident adult trainees can recognize tide and practice supervised turns with Shellbend/Crescent host-pilots. Four-person hull completed supervised sheltered-coast hop, still not endorsed for distant exposed coast; staged testing and crew rescue planning active.

research_in_progress.name: Year13 exploration vessel Reedwing: final northward seaworthiness and repair readiness
research_in_progress.stage: Year12 Day187: fitted and short-route tested with cargo, improved stability and return drills; test through difficult Crescent tidal cut and full provisions/crew in good weather after host confirmation in Year13. Four planned expedition adults; no long-range departure in Year12.

research_in_progress.name: Reedwing expedition aftermath and northern coast pilot knowledge
research_in_progress.stage: Year13 Day47: long-range voyage completed and four crew safely returned. Inspect cargo bracing, freshwater/provision losses, paddle repairs and route observations before next voyage; do not presume beyond-inlet passage rights or open-ocean capability.

research_in_progress.name: Ternhook community relationships and northern river-mouth hypothesis
research_in_progress.stage: Year13 Days26-31: tentative first meeting with welcoming local shore fishers after direct permission at one beach; seasonal fish weirs and broad drift material seen, northern river outflow hypothesized but not explored; future contact only by invitation.

research_in_progress.name: Tidefin second sea-capable vessel qualification
research_in_progress.stage: COMPLETED Year13 Days161-191: Tidefin made first consented north-route full load and return in safe-weather two-vessel convoy with Reedwing, Keshu pilot assisting. Stable lashing after prelaunch repair, successful Crescent tidal crossing and Ternhook return, regular posttrip inspection. Qualified on proven coastal route under comparable safeguards, not open-ocean travel.

research_in_progress.name: Second Ternhook contact and possible future bilateral coastal trade
research_in_progress.stage: Year13 Days171-218: third invited Ternhook landing, fish-hook net-tool barter and host demonstration on stone tidal-weir maintenance; visiting adults later reciprocally attended one Taluma market through Crescent escort. Tentative seasonal notice and invitation protocol, separately agreed for each meeting; no binding treaty/common fluency or permanent shore rights.

research_in_progress.name: Maintainable two-boat northern coastal service
research_in_progress.stage: Year13 Day227: both Reedwing and Tidefin returned seaworthy after host-permitted convoy, crews have incident/inspection and abort records. Continue paired navigator training and postvoyage hull inspection; qualification limited to known coastal route in suitable conditions.

research_in_progress.name: Southern coastal route reconnaissance and possible first contact
research_in_progress.stage: Year13 Day302: Windcut Bay offshore-only survey beyond southern Shellbend; investigate shifting sandbar/possible local users only with fresh host agreement, deliberate diplomacy and favorable weather. No assumption of empty land.

research_in_progress.stage: Year14 Day19 three sheets completed; Maro/Leni train apprentices to revise safely using eyewitness notes and host-provided warnings, not fabricated distances.

research_in_progress.name: Northern estuary follow-up
