Year4 Day191: Corun and Seli began separate trials for cleaner roof rain: divert the first dirty wash, settle and strain visible grit, boil later captured water in clay vessels, and cool covered using cleaned implements. Heating revealed that some fired clay cups still crack or leak; no automatic potable status was granted.

Year4 Day207: Nine of twelve small rainwater batches completed sustained rolling boil and clean covered transfer; two pots cracked and one batch was discarded after dirty handling. Some water was used promptly in supervised household trials without immediate visible illness; this does not prove long-term health safety. Material and fuel costs entered in ledger.

Year4 Day214: Maro and Leni found five early unfired record trials damaged by a leaking roof; this prompted Arel to build raised shelves, stone-backed dry bins and covered storage. Nine harder fired exemplar tablets and twelve dry working records survived later checks.

Year4 Day225: Hall of Many Hands formally opened its permanent practical archive. Maro and Vessa agreed on an oral witness for household and stores entries, copying crucial water and food tallies and comparing records by independent readers. Names and complex stories remain oral, not phonetic script.

Year4 Day236: two useful rainwater collector lines were operating and the previously isolated line underwent repair for trial only. Corun continued to measure water drawn from the existing protected spring separately from experimental rain; historical low 82 daily shares versus 74 residents remains the growth constraint.

Year4 Day240: 65-day ledger at 74 residents. Food66−65+70−1 hospitality−2 spoilage=68 days (four earmarked care); fuel58−65+12 measured savings−4 heating/firing+61 lawful collection=62 days. Materials poles25+3−2=26; reeds39+6−5=40; stone4+1−1=4; cordage7+2−2=7; clay2+3−4=1. Future family-home materials and protected seeds untouched. No population or housing change.

Year4 Day241: guiding intelligence explicitly postponed outer freshwater survey at Northfold and other sites, instead ordered improved rain treatment, family names/lineage records, and expeditions seeking other peaceful communities and new trade partners.

Year4 Days247-286: Corun, Iren and Seli trialed pre-warmed thickened boiling pots and vented lids; eight of ten small comparable water batches completed disciplined boil/clean-covered prompt-use procedure. One pot cracked, one transfer was dirty and batch discarded. Approx 20% less firewood in successful comparable batches than first tests, too limited to certify long-term safe or scalable supply.

Year4 Day271: Letha and Sena scouts reached northern Reedmouth Inlet beyond Longbank, not via paused Northfold water survey. Three coastal adults used reed float-lines and bone awls near a likely seasonal camp; occupation recognized, no local rights assumed.
Year4 Day282: first distant greeting at Reedmouth Inlet was reciprocated on open sand, scouting party withdrew without approaching fishers work or homes.

Year4 Day286: Maro and Leni spotted two unrelated people assigned accidentally same personal mark while preparing family records; separate sign conventions developed, spoken names still checked with witnesses.

Year4 Day293: six household genealogy tiles and four fired exemplars placed in Hall archive; descriptions pair conventional personal tokens and parent/child or household relations. Rema/Jorin/Nala, Anet/Boran/Tavi and Sena/Daro/Tiri among witnessed families, not an alphabet or exhaustive family tree.

Year4 Day298: second Reedmouth meeting at host-approved open beach produced one inspected, voluntary exchange of Taluman cordage coil for worked bone awl. No treaty, guaranteed future visit, shared name, invitation into camp, or land/resource right.

Year4 Day303: 63-day resource ledger, 74 people unchanged, housing81: food68−63+68−1 gift−1 hospitality−1 spoilage=70; fuel62−63+11 measured savings−3 boiling/archive firing+59 lawful gathering=66. Materials P26+4−2=28; R40+7−4=43; S4+1−1=4; C7+3−1 exchange−1 used=8; clay1+4−3=2. Future-home and caregiver stock earmarks, four food care-days and survival seed2 protected. Remote water search paused while local spring monitoring continued.
Year4 Day313: Letha and Sena prepared a pictorial, verbal invitation at outer Reedmouth beach for a voluntary short craft visit, with no requests to enter their camp. Visitors made no promise yet.

Year4 Days320-326: after a second open-shore encounter, two Reedmouth craftspeople agreed to travel with escorts to Taluma Hall on Days339-341; explicit but one-time consent and free departure preserved.

Year4 Day331: Council and Vessa adopted a seasonal Shore Walk tradition: two to four consenting adult scouts at safe low tide and in fair weather, carrying enough provisions, returning with knowledge and warnings; no claiming land or cutting occupied traps.

Year4 Days339-341: two Reedmouth craftspeople taught net float cordage adjustment and bone awl repair during a voluntary 3-day visit. Taluma shared roof-drainage and pottery knowledge; guests rejected guarantee of recurring future appointments and went home. One witnessed trade involved a coil of cordage, one treated clay pot and food gifts in existing ledger; no migration.

Year4 Days347-350: Sena and Nemi tested Reedmouth-style floats in Taluma lagoon only. First line caught too much wind/current and net tangled; revised weights improved position in ordinary tide but catch benefit not measured. Crafts students watched safety demonstrations.

Year4 Day356: Letha led first longer recurring Shore Walk north of Reedmouth. Scouts stopped before a dangerous rising-tide cut and spotted smoke beyond farther shoals; no closer approach, unknown source and no new people confirmed.

Year5 Day3: Maro archived initial coast travel tokens and an oral account of Reedmouth visit. Young apprentices asked whether signs could indicate whether a route is safe at high or low tide; independently readable proto-writing remains incomplete.

Year5 Day10: 72-day summary, population74 housing81 unchanged. Food70−72+78−2 exchange−1 hospitality−1 spoilage=72; fuel66−72+14 hearth/shelter savings−2 boiling/firing+65 collected=71. Materials: poles28+4−1=31; reeds43+6−4=45; stones4+1−1=4; cordage8+3−1 traded−1 used=9; clay2+3−2=3. Protected emergency seeds, family house and care reserves intact. Remote independent freshwater survey still suspended.

Year5 Day18: Corun and Seli reviewed water records on rainfall-independent spring flow; spring remains only ordinary drinking supply. Approved local nonpotable roof runoff work and cautious prompt-use boiled rain trials, with clean handling and extra fuel costs.

Year5 Day23: Reedmouth coastal fisher voluntarily met Letha and Sena at neutral shore and showed reed float arrangements that change when fish return with seasonal tides; gestures indicated occasional work movement to farther shore and seasonal drying.

Year5 Days24-38: paired adults watched lagoon high and low reference marks through one moon change. Maro and Leni refined tide pictograms and oral return-warning instructions. Marks placed only on Taluma-used approaches; no claim at Reedmouth.

Year5 Day31: Corun resumes non-extractive Northfold observations after player explicitly rescinded remote survey pause by ordering water problem solved. Seep continued to trickle; cautious reconnaissance only, no drawing for drinking.

Year5 Days38-45: another voluntary Reedmouth meeting arranged a single guided observation from the safe shoreward side of northern shoals. Smoke beyond outer point linked by hosts to their intermittent fish-drying work, not proven fourth people. Adults returned before high tide; specific travel permission ended.

Year5 Days41-55: in a relatively dry run, measured Taluma spring provisional low fell to79 daily resident-equivalent shares, leaving just5 above current74 residents. Year5 Day54: third total Northfold observation including latest two turns shows water after roughly14 rain-poor days, but tiny flow, possible human footprints, uncertain hygiene, ownership and independent aquifer. Party left without collecting or installing any works.

Year5 Day58: strong onshore winds drove an early surge over expected shore-walk low-route window. Scout team turned back and revised witnessed warnings. No casualties or crossing of occupied grounds; tides are not perfectly predictable.

Year5 Day68: council summary after58 days, population74 housing81 unchanged, food72−58+64−2 hospitality−1 spoilage=75; fuel71−58+12 savings−3 boiling/firing+53 legally gathered=75. Roof rain catch110 large jugs,68 useful nonpotable,22 boiled prompt-use batches,20 lost/rejected. Protected seed and family care/housing stocks intact. Year5 Day80: Letha and Corun approached the Northfold seep users only after checking the open margin and finding a Reedmouth-associated intermediary; separate introductory gestures produced no immediate right to use water.
Year5 Day87: Reedmouth and Taluma first tried a witnessed pictorial seasonal meeting marker at neutral sand, establishing a custom of proposing a next meeting, not a permanent binding schedule.

Year5 Day96: blocked first-flush reed screen in the newly expanded roof rain channels ruined a partly filled covered basin batch; Corun isolated and discarded it, then revised the replaceable upstream trap.
Year5 Day104: first specific escorted Northfold observational visit granted by local seasonal users; Corun watched the runnel and recorded its flow without sampling or altering bank.
Year5 Day111: Taluma Hall welcomed a separate Reedmouth group for storm-surge warnings, craft and reed-float knot study. Guests departed freely; a future request must be accepted anew.
Year5 Day119: second and final permitted Northfold field observation, one-off escort expired; seasonal hosts indicated possible warm-season low water, with meaning uncertain; no extraction rights.

Year5 Day129: winter council reckoning: 74 people and81 housing spaces; food72 and fuel70 settlement-days. Larger nonpotable rain capacity ~48 jugloads; in 61 days135 captured,82 useful nonpotable,28 boiled/promptly consumed as carefully treated trial,18 lost/ discarded,7 stored nonpotable. Northfold unqualified for population expansion; seasonal Reedmouth learning exchange voluntary.

Year5 Day140: Vessa and Iren began low-fuel water-treatment pot and prewarming trials at Taluma sheltered workshop. Ten test vessels across the interval, seven survived firing; five completed initial boiling/cooling/clean-transfer cycle, with fuel per usable small jug around25% below earlier trials in matched conditions. No guaranteed safe long-term storage.
Year5 Day149: first of four host-consented Northfold visual water watches, with Corun and Letha and two Reedmouth-connected seasonal users. No water taken or site changed.
Year5 Day164: second Northfold escorted visual observation; water still visibly runs, signs of flow variability recorded in pictographic observations.

Year5 Day171-172: Hall of Many Hands hosted two Reedmouth, one Shellbend and one inland craft teacher by individual invitation. Shared reed repair, wind/tide warning, clay temper and shelter methods. Shellbend visitor declined to disclose a weir detail; the choice was respected. All guests departed freely.
Year5 Day178: third Northfold permitted observation after fluctuating weather, led to careful record comparison but no proof of dry-season supply.

Year5 Day185: Sora and apprentices sorted a small harvested wild-grass batch suitable for limited food use, part of normal settlement food production; protected seed selected for future trials still untouched. No food-scale farming transition.

Year5 Day190: fourth and final escorted Northfold survey saw a narrower trickle after relative dryness. Host warning about late warm-season near-cessation possible but interpretation uncertain; all observation permissions expired without drawing water or claiming land.

Year5 Day194: winter council: 74 residents, 81 housing places; food74 fuel68 days. No births/deaths/migration; water capacity spring79 observed low against74 demand, Northfold unqualified, roof-water nonpotable capacity48 jugs. Shared Hall meeting and improved small-batch heating completed; reserved two-house materials, family supplies and protected seeds intact.

Year5 Day215: Corun, Seli, Iren and Vessa enrolled six volunteer households in supervised small batch water boiling and cleaned covered handling; preliminary training exposed challenges from cracks and recontamination, not replacement for main spring.

Year5 Day271: in a record-copying session Leni noticed a tide-warning technique credited to Taluma had first been shown by Reedmouth travelers. Maro arranged verification by community signs and witnesses rather than insisting on Taluman authorship.

Year5 Days281-282: annual Meeting of Many Hands returned, including invited representatives of Reedmouth, Shellbend and inland people. Teachers chose what to disclose. Seven witness-checked attribution tiles prepared; the tide-warning credit error corrected in public, teaching provenance became a custom.

Year5 Day292: Yana, a previously unnamed pre-existing adult net-repair worker, bore daughter Eri with Seli providing care; her partner Ilo, an existing adult shore gatherer, joined her in household care. Taluma population grew from74 to75, no outside immigration.

Year5 Day302: at user-authorized final escorted warm-season Northfold observation, Corun and Letha saw a few damp pockets but virtually no continuously running surface water. No extraction/claim; host escort expired. By express player instruction, Northfold investigation ended and no further attempts will be made absent new specific player orders.

Year5 Day320: household experiment summary 48 small jug batches,36 completed careful heat/clean covering/short-use and12 rejected, four additional fuel-days; no certified safe storage or year-round water. Council reports75 residents,81 housing, food75 and fuel72 days; old home/family earmarks and seed intact.

Year5 Day331: council instituted staged dry-weather water warnings, distinguishing must-have drinking/hygiene from optional spring draws for crafts; existing main spring monitored without outside expeditions.

Year5 Day344: temporary low-rain interval showed spring near78 daily shares; Corun maintained essential draws and shifted discretionary tool washing to remaining approved nonpotable storage. No family refused critical drinking or hygiene.

Year5 Day353: after16 particularly dry observational days, Corun recorded minimum near76 daily resident-equivalent shares while Taluma housed75. Council suspended optional spring cleaning, stopped accepting new residents and retained conservative water status; no Northfold contact.

Year5 Day360: Vessa and Iren compared five clay lids/lining choices; three resisted obvious seepage for four days, one cracked, one resin-treated vessel developed suspect smell and water discarded. Resin kept off drinking vessel interiors; leak tightness not considered potable safety.

Year6 Day9: first heavy rain after dry spell fed Taluma-local roof-fed covered catchments; new12-jug compartment brought total simultaneous nonpotable capacity to60. Across turn 90 large jugloads collected:61 useful for crafts and cleaning,15 boiled and immediately used in small supervised trials,14 discarded or lost; no full-drought drinking buffer proven.

Year6 Day13: Maro, Vessa and Leni trialed four marks combining personal-household determinatives with recurring spoken sound chunks; two were reliably interpreted by learners only when familiar oral names were supplied. A name confusion exposed weakness, no true phonetic writing claimed.

Year6 Day18: with consenting relatives and safe escorts, two older Shellbend children and one Reedmouth young learner visited Hall of Many Hands for one day and returned; Taluman children learned buoyancy with bowls and guests showed their own knot-fastening practice. No foreign visitors included in census.

Year6 Day29: Council reports Taluma enters sixth year at population75, housing81, food78/fuel74 settlement-days, spring dry lowest76 daily shares, built nonpotable rain-capacity60 large jugs; family housing reserve and seed2 intact. Northfold permanently CLOSED absent specific player reversal.

Year6 Day41: after one proposed water allotment ignored household size and care needs, Seli challenged the initial equal-household measure; Corun and Maro began drafting individual essential-needs water shares and witnessed shortfall alerts with council review, protecting drinking, care and hygiene.

Year6 Day47: Council of the Shore approved Agreement of the Spring. Low-water observation at <=3 spare daily shares triggers public warning, witnessed household share marks, independent review of mistakes, suspension of optional spring draws, and no mass immigration. Prioritize health and individualized care; no coercive neglect of children or elders.

Year6 Day52: Leni asked whether a roof not attached to a house might capture rain. Arel and Tama constructed two tilted removable woven-reed rain collectors on Taluma land near existing drainage; one diverted first dusty runoff safely from spring.

Year6 Day66: wind tore loose one stand-alone collector and flattened it; nobody harmed. Another held with extra bracing and weighted footings; damaged unit dismantled rather than left unsafe. Arel required a wind test in the building standards before further expansion.

Year6 Day78: connected successful pitched catchment to a new covered24-jug clay basin, raising peak nonpotable covered storage to84 jugloads from60. Several rainy episodes brought160 collected jugs; 104 used for tools, cleaning and clay;20 promptly boiled and supervised for use;25 discarded or lost;11 nonpotable jugs remaining. Source spring remains the only routine drinking supply.

Year6 Day91: a family questioned a posted distribution tally that counted children as full adult needs but overlooked nursing and illness. Seli and Maro corrected the witnessed entry after listening, illustrating why drought rules must allow review. No dehydration crisis; spring flow above essential demand during this period, dry recorded low76 versus75 residents; drought remains an unsolved long-term risk.

Year6 Day95: Taluma reports population75, housing81, food82 days, fuel75 days, nonpotable peak storage84 jugs; reserve for two future homes and family care intact. Northfold remained entirely closed under player instruction. Free-standing collector proven in ordinary rain after one storm failure, not all-weather nor potable.

Year6 Day107: Arel and Tama constructed two additional independent pitched reed catchers on Taluma-used ground, steering first dirty runoff out and later runoff into screened nonpotable storage. Separate 16+16 jug covered basins increased system capacity from84 to116 jugloads. Dry-season drought solution not claimed.

Year6 Day111: council with Corun and Seli established the Rain Hands: each household asked to share responsibility for rainwater maintenance through appropriate physical labor, materials, recording, replacement of covers or caregiving support. Need-based exceptions and alternative contributions guaranteed; access to essential spring water remains unconditional.

Year6 Day132: first common Water Hands day: adults inspected covers and wind-braces, household recorders compared retained-jug tallies and older apprentices taught younger people only safe cordage and counting tasks. A caregiver questioned equal hours; Seli established alternative caregiving as equal contribution. No children on high structures or in hot-water handling.

Year6 Day139: one newly built pitched rain collector sagged under accumulated rain, driving dirty overflow toward a clean-lined basin. Corun isolated and rejected water before anyone used it. Arel and Tama re-tensioned supports, redirected spill bypass and re-tested on Day143. No drinking water contaminated; severe wind endurance still unknown.

Year6 Day135-169: Sora, with six rotating capable adults and apprentices, prepared a 24x40-pace common field using Taluma-local permitted soil and previously selected trial grass seed. Dark mulched strips emerged better, exposed sandy edges attracted birds. Earlier mature demonstration plots provided two settlement-day food-equivalents included in the standard fish/gathering/crop total; new common field remains immature. Protected survival seed2 untouched.

Year6 Day166: council tallied 205 large jugloads captured across showers:139 used for cleaning/clay/craft work,25 supervised boiled and promptly used,31 lost or rejected,10 left covered for nonpotable uses. Covered peak capacity now116, three independent collectors operational after repairs. Spring historical minimum76 versus75 resident demand unchanged, 100-person target gated.

Year6 Day169: Taluma 75 inhabitants (44 adults,24 children,7 elders), housing81, food80 days, fuel77 days. Every household participates in Water Hands with flexible fair roles; the experimental common field is not yet a staple. Home reserve for two planned shelters and family-care material allotments preserved. Northfold received NO visits, surveys, inquiries or work.

Year6 Days179-199: Sora and Corun ran four small comparable field strips on already permitted common plot, two watered with24 jugloads of captured nonpotable rain (within163 nonpotable period uses) and two rain-fed controls. By harvest watered strips measured31 standardized handfuls of dry seed heads vs23 on controls; variation and unreplicated small sample noted. No spring draw for irrigation.

Year6 Day204: first large wind-driven storm tested 40-jug new covered stone/clay cistern. A long seam seeped; catchment bypass diverted suspect runoff, escaped water discarded. Arel and Tama strengthened removable repair joint and tested at partial capacity in ordinary rain Day219; no full-storm approval. New theoretical max covered NONPOTABLE capacity156 jugloads.

Year6 Day225: Rema and Jorin welcomed second child Neru, younger sibling of Nala, attended by Seli. Population75->76, children24->25, adults44/elders7 unchanged, housing81. Spring historic low76 shares/day now matches resident number, no observed safety margin.

Year6 Day236: first Gathering of Seed Heads and annual First Furrow seasonal practice inaugurated, with Maro/Leni and apprentices recording actual grain, seed retention and teachers. Sora common field edible harvest3 food-day equivalents and mature older experimental beds1, already in period gross production82; no staple-scale breakthrough.

Year6 Day245: 76-day close. Community Water Hands continues with every household contributing in appropriate capacity and no withheld essentials. Rain collected244 jugs (163 nonpotable uses, 27 supervised boiled immediate uses,43 discarded/leaked,11 covered nonpotable remainder). Food82 days, fuel81 days, population76, housing81, home/family/seed reserves intact. NORTHFOLD COMPLETELY CLOSED.

Year6 Day258: Esha approved no-deep-digging groundwater investigation on existing Taluma-used land only, away from latrine runoff, protected spring and high-tide flood zones; Arel, Corun and Letha prescribed guarded/shored shallow probes, no people entering unsafe pits or drinking untested water.

Year6 Day262: first coastal shallow exploratory pit revealed wet sand closely following tidal height; tiny retained water deposit dried to visibly crystalline residue compared with fresh spring control, likely brackish tidal seepage. Pit covered/closed without drinking or water supply credit. Leni helped compare tide observation marks.

Year6 Day276: severe squall opened part of 40-jug cistern removable cover; overflow led safely away, basin structure and repairable seam held, but grit fouled 12 jug-loads which were discarded. Arel/Tama reinforced lashings and debris bypass after review by Corun.

Year6 Day281: Sora separated 24 plump mature selected grain seeds and24 smaller seeds, planted matched shallow trays in comparable conditions; only seed produced by prior experiments was used, not protected two food-day seed. Apprentices and Leni recorded which sprouted, keeping plots labeled.

Year6 Day291: second shallow, safely braced test on locally permitted land farther back from coast found slow cloudy seep after rains; no permanent well, no drinking withdrawal, no evidence of dry-season flow or aquifer independence from spring. Perimeter covered and marked, tests will remain nonpotable unless evidence warrants careful next step. Northfold not visited.

Year6 Day301: after reinforced cover test, major storm produced ~35 jugs held in trial cistern without visible seam leak or loose lid; still only storm-resilience evidence, not potable safety or complete long-term reliability.

Year6 Day309: Sora tallied17/24 sprouted selected plump-seed trials and11/24 smaller-head control seeds. Planting of tiny next-season comparison strips prepared, no mature grain yield from them yet; older established beds contributed about2 settlement food-days within77 total produced.

Year6 Day317: 72-day close. Population76, housing81. Food82->84, fuel81->82. Both local test pits safeguarded, zero new potable shares; Northfold categorically CLOSED. All future-house and family-care/seed reserves intact.
Year6 Day329: Letha and Sena confirmed long-standing Shore Walks continue, two permitted coasts surveyed with tide warnings, no encroachment on neighbor works or Northfold.

Year6 Day340: Arel and Tama completed first standardized 24-jug storm-braced removable-covered NONPOTABLE cistern; during later squall lid shifted, dirty contents among57 period losses rejected, repair and reinspection followed.
Year6 Day351: Corun first warm dry-ground checks of guarded landward Taluma shallow seep; moisture weakens after rainfall ceases. No drinking or deeper digging.
Year6 Day363: annual witnessed sow/soil observances continued, seed-origin records include contributions from Reedmouth/Shellbend/inland craftspeople with permission and credits.

Year7 Day16-20: voluntary two-day Hall teaching exchange with visiting Reedmouth and Shellbend children/carers and inland fiberworker. Leni corrects a spoken-name sound-mark mishearing; no full phonetic script. Visitors leave safely.

Year7 Day21-56: two adult Shore Walks and one consented reciprocal Reedmouth meeting observe unfamiliar polished greenish pebble from indirect exchange; provenance and farther people unknown. No new group formally contacted or route claimed.
