unresolved_threads: The completed four-visit timber pilot brought temporary relief, but no continuing inland access was secured; how should Taluma sustain firewood supply without assuming renewal?
Would the inland people consider a new voluntary exchange in the future? No standing access or treaty exists, and Taluma must never presume consent from the expired pilot.
Can Sora gather enough seeds from the small spring seedheads to support a meaningful trial plot later without using protected seed?
Will a fuller season of cooking-hearth use confirm small but valuable wood savings, and is safe scale-up possible with available stone and labor?
Can Corun maintain reliable water delivery during future warm and dry periods?
Can Nemi keep food protection robust during humid weather without losing grain or fish stores?
Who constructed or tends the stone tidal barrier at Shellbend Cove, and can Taluma safely use nearby shore resources without conflict?
Can shared cooking and permitted coastal fuel fully offset daily wood consumption before depleted coastal stands force a hard tradeoff?
Who are the active Shellbend Cove weir-tenders? Can Letha learn their name or establish welcome contact without disrupting their fishery?
Will the strongest of Sora's three cultivation beds eventually produce enough recoverable seed to justify labor beyond observation?
Can Letha learn how the Shellbend coastal people organize their fish-weir work, and are they willing to discuss seasonal cooperation without access concessions?
Can Vessa turn the first porous low-fired pots into consistently durable vessels without unsustainable firing fuel?
Will the Circle of Witnesses preserve reliable seasonal knowledge after older witnesses die, and how should conflicting accounts be handled?
Will Shellbend fishers volunteer further technical instruction or nonbinding cooperation? No ongoing fishery or landing rights exist; their own working stones are still off-limits.
Can the new Taluma pottery workshop reliably make waterproof, durable vessels at a fuel and breakage cost the village can sustain through winter?
How will Rema and Jorin adapt to caring for newborn Nala, and will a second generation of Talumans grow within the available housing and spring capacity?
Will Taluma's own removable tidal fish guide survive stronger winter tides and justify a larger cooperative fishery without interfering with others?
Can the council maintain fuel above 30-day minimum during further pottery firing and wood scarcity, or must it slow ceramics?
Will the neighboring craftspeople return voluntarily, and can Taluma deepen relationships without jumping to premature treaties or inaccurate translations?
How quickly will small clay and stone sources deplete under workshop and fish-trap needs?
Can Taluma make tidal traps robust enough in storms without trapping too many juvenile fish or reducing future catches?
Can the coastal hauling route support larger clay/stone needs without damaging the shore or overburdening adult labor?
Will voluntary Open Learning Days develop capable future teachers over the years rather than treating young people as instant labor?
Will winter firewood stay above minimum if the pottery workshop expands?

Is the western dune trickle fed by the same groundwater as the northern protected spring, or could it provide a dependable independent backup? How safe is collected rainwater without boiling and storage protection?
Can Taluma sustain the Hall of Many Hands and its teaching schedule without consuming too much construction stock or leaving too little labor for the now 32-day fuel reserve?
Will visiting coast and inland craftspeople continue to attend voluntarily when winter trade, crops and household demands compete for their time?
Can the one functioning roof-fed rainwater basin stay sealed and clean in hotter weather, and can Taluma develop genuinely safe non-spring drinking water without contamination?
Will inland and Shellbend visitors choose to return for the next annual Meeting of Many Hands, or will seasonal and diplomatic pressures change the tradition?
Will the newly found Western Gravel Run stay active during the driest season, and could water be transported and made safe without relying on the same threatened aquifer?
Will neighboring communities continue willingly to use observed reciprocal pebble counts, or will disagreements about basket size, quality and value reveal the limits of the emerging barter custom?
Will Western Gravel Run maintain adequate safe independent water through its driest period, and is the gravel bench free of dangerous floods and active neighboring use?
Will a recurring Taluma trade gathering remain mutually beneficial without uniform standards, and can neighbors settle disputes about size or spoilage without coercion?
Can the council responsibly prepare more housing and dependable freshwater capacity for newly invited settlers and naturally growing families, now with 71 people and only two spare shelter places?
Does Longbank Terrace have reliable safe drinking water and sufficiently stable soils, seasonal shelter and no conflicting use to make an independent outpost sensible?
Will a repeatable basket measure remain fair for trades with variable contents, without becoming coercive or creating unauthorized external rules?
Can fitted low-fired pottery survive long dry-seed storage and bad weather, with fuel expenses low enough to expand production?
Will the protected upper spring maintain safe flow for 73 current residents and future children through the next dry season, or must Taluma discover a truly independent potable source?
Can Taluma eventually sustain more births and invited residents without exhausting food, lawful fuel, caretaker time and housing even after the recent eight-place expansion?
Can reed weaving and carried-water innovations taught by new residents become durable, locally teachable skills without treating their former community as an economic dependency?
Will Anet and Boran choose to become parents in future years, and can the council maintain safe birth, child and elder support without treating family relationships as compulsory?
Will the roof and entrance insulation pilot remain dry and ventilated through storms, and can its measurable extra warmth scale without exceeding lawful reed supplies?
Before any sustained population growth to 100, can Corun confirm source recharge through dry and storm seasons, and can the council supply 37% greater safe freshwater draw and handling?
Will the Roof-Raising Day and Night of Shared Fires endure as useful inclusive household traditions and lead to sustainable multigenerational changes rather than just symbolic festivities?
Will Taluma identify a safe, independent additional source or reduce water losses enough to support population 100 during the harshest dry season, beyond the measured low 86 person-shares per day?
Will new raised woven sleeping mats and removable wall sections stay dry and smoke-safe through an actual hard storm without consuming unrenewable reed stocks?
When cured materials become available, will actual household demand and verified safe water justify the first of two reserved family shelters?
Will optional adult shelter apprenticeships with Shellbend and inland hosts develop into a reciprocal, mutually permitted learning relationship without assuming access rights?
Will Anet’s early signs prove to be a pregnancy, and can Seli provide care and privacy regardless of outcome?
Can the main spring recharge sufficiently after the dry spell, or will Taluma need a separate independently verified source before any major new residents?
Can Vessa and Corun produce a truly dependable covered drinking-water storage technique without slow spoilage, and when would it warrant an actual reserve?
Will an extended real storm test confirm whether neighbors’ adjustable drainage and removable wall systems improve safe household resilience without sealing smoke outlets?
Will Anet’s likely early pregnancy progress safely under Seli’s care, and how will Boran and their household prepare?

Will Anet deliver safely in the coming season, and will the reserve and repaired homes meet the needs of growing families?
Can the annual winter storms validate three new retrofits and the five common building checks without excessive fuel and materials expense?
Can pottery improve enough for dependable boiling vessels and hygienic, fuel-efficient same-day cooled storage, especially when winter fuel is scarce and rains stop?
Will Taluma develop symbols for spoken names, relationships and sequence that can be independently read, rather than only household tokens and counted goods?

Can Taluma build a durable, reciprocal tradition of visiting-child learning while honoring neighboring parents, guardians, and teacher consent?

gameplay_mode.governance: Council autonomously manages all existing permanent survival duties without repeat orders
gameplay_mode.default_on_next_or_continue: Adaptive multiweek progress, often several weeks; longer for quiet periods, shorter for significant player-only decisions. No rigid jump size.
gameplay_mode.response_policy: Narrate consequential developments and show a compact dashboard. Offer only a handful of genuinely timely, nonduplicative strategic suggestions, often ~3-4 but never a fixed quota; always also Continue and unrestricted custom orders. event_driven_pacing.normal_horizon: Adaptive weeks to months. Do not impose a fixed 10, 30, 45 or 90-day span.
interrupt_early_for: immediate serious threat or emergency beyond council remit
warfare, binding treaty, territorial claims, major migration or other irreversible sovereign choice
genuinely transformative discovery posing a time-sensitive major choice
high-stakes institutional or political crossroads requiring player direction
do_not_interrupt_for: ordinary visitors or routine follow-on contact
simple nonverbal gestures or unverified small discoveries
every stage of an ongoing research or diplomacy chain
manufactured cliffhangers or choices safely resolved by delegates
event_driven_pacing.on_early_stop: Stop at event day only when player agency genuinely needed, preserve unelapsed horizon, update checkpoint
event_driven_pacing.on_quiet_turn: Progress substantially; summarize several events without forcing choice

gameplay_mode.player_agency: Frequent, substantive player direction across several domains; multi-select options and unrestricted freeform orders, with council autonomously implementing persistent goals. Do not reduce user to spectator.
gameplay_mode.progression: Cumulative project milestones, evolving characters and plausible demographics; neither frozen population nor forced artificial progress; auditable resource ledger.

cordage.participants: Vessa, Tira, Maren, Dava and consenting fiber apprentices
cordage.method: Comparable locally prepared two-ply, closely braided three-strand, and stiffened-fiber lashings tested under repeated wetting and abrasive sand contact using existing frames and clay witness tallies. Two of five first tightly braided samples loosened after wetting; knots redesigned, subsequent samples lasted longer in supervised local trials but still show fraying.
cordage.proven: More consistent supervised local manufacture of nine standard-size cordage coils, a repeatable abrasion-test setup, and a promising but imperfect alternate braid.
cordage.unproven: No full Windcut storm-season performance, no universal advantage, and no new bulk export guarantee. Five coils consumed destructively in trials; three in ordinary repairs.
cordage.costs: Two poles and seven reed bundles to trial work (poles include building a drying rack), five cordage coils in tests, ten fuel-day equivalents within accounting; the supervision reduced available boatyard craft hours, but safety maintenance was not postponed.
